questions.question: Which of the following regions is known to receive the maximum rainfall from the South-west Monsoon winds in India?

__
 
• The **Western Ghats** receive the maximum rainfall from the South-west Monsoon winds in India.
 
• This mountain range runs parallel to the western coast of the Indian peninsula and significantly influences the monsoon patterns.
 
• The Western Ghats are known for their rich biodiversity and are recognized as one of the world's eight "hottest hotspots" of biological diversity.
 
• Regions such as **Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu** benefit from the heavy rainfall brought by the South-west Monsoon.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The South-west Monsoon typically arrives in India around early June and lasts until September, bringing the majority of the country's annual rainfall.
 
• The monsoon is crucial for agriculture in India, as it directly impacts the water supply for irrigation and reservoirs.
 
• Areas like **Cherrapunji and Mawsynram** in Meghalaya, although not part of the Western Ghats, are also known for receiving extremely high rainfall during the monsoon season.
 
• The Western Ghats not only contribute to rainfall distribution but also play a significant role in the climate and weather patterns of the Indian subcontinent.

questions.question: A tank is filled in 4 hours by three pipes A, B and C. Pipe C is twice as fast as pipe B and pipe B is twice as fast as pipe A. How much time will pipe A take to fill the tank?
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

Let the efficiency of pipe A be 1 unit/hour

Efficiency of pipe B = 2 units/hour

Efficiency of C = 4 units/hour

Total efficiency of A, B, and C = 1 + 2 + 4 = 7

They finish in 4 hours

⇒ Total work = (1 + 2 + 4) × 4 = 28 units

Pipe A alone can fill the whole tank in = 28/1 = 28 hrs.

**∴ Option 2 is the correct answer.**

__
 
• The angle of deviation is the angle between the incident ray and the emergent ray.
 
• In a prism, the ray of light bends twice, once when it enters the prism and once when it exits.
 
• The angle of deviation depends on the angle of incidence, the refractive index of the prism material, and the angle of the prism.
 
• The angle of deviation is minimum when the angle of incidence is such that the light ray passes symmetrically through the prism.

• **Snell's Law**

 
 
• It describes how light bends when it passes from one medium to another.
 
• It is given by the formula: *n1 * sin(θ1) = n2 * sin(θ2)*, where n1 and n2 are the refractive indices of the two media, and θ1 and θ2 are the angles of incidence and refraction, respectively.
 
 
 
• **Refractive Index**
 
 
• The refractive index of a medium is a measure of how much it can bend light.
 
• It is defined as the ratio of the speed of light in a vacuum to the speed of light in the medium.
 
 
 
• **Prism Formula**
 
 
• The relationship between the angle of incidence, angle of refraction, and the angle of the prism can be described using the prism formula: *A = r1 + r2*, where A is the angle of the prism and r1 and r2 are the angles of refraction at the two surfaces of the prism.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution specifically mentions, "The official language of the Union shall be Hindi in Devanagari script?"

__
 
• **Article 343(1)** of the Indian Constitution specifies that "The official language of the Union shall be Hindi in Devanagari script."
 
• The Constitution initially provided for the continued use of English for all official purposes of the Union for a period of 15 years from its commencement, after which Hindi was to become the sole official language.
 
• However, due to the linguistic diversity of India, the Official Languages Act, 1963 was passed, allowing for the continued use of English alongside Hindi for official purposes.
 
• This provision highlights the importance of Hindi as the official language, while also recognizing the practical need for English in official communication.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949** and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written** constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• The **Official Languages Act, 1963** plays a crucial role in the continued use of English for official purposes, reflecting the linguistic diversity of the nation.

__
 
• The main aim of the agreement made by UNEP in 1987 was **to freeze the production of CFCs at the 1986 level**.
 
• This agreement is known as the **Montreal Protocol** on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer.
 
• The protocol was designed to protect the ozone layer by phasing out the production of numerous substances responsible for ozone depletion, primarily chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs).
 
• The Montreal Protocol is considered one of the most successful environmental agreements to date.

• The **United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP)** facilitated the Montreal Protocol, which was agreed upon on **September 16, 1987**, and entered into force on **January 1, 1989**.
 
• As of today, the protocol has undergone several amendments and adjustments to include more substances and to accelerate the phase-out schedules.
 
• The Montreal Protocol has significantly contributed to the recovery of the ozone layer and is a model for international cooperation on environmental issues.
 
• Due to its success, September 16 is celebrated as **International Day for the Preservation of the Ozone Layer**.

__

questions.question: ________ determines the sex of fertilised eggs in a few reptiles.

• In contrast, in genetic sex determination systems, such as those in humans, sex is determined at fertilization by the combination of sex chromosomes (XX for females and XY for males).

• International organizations, such as the United Nations, advocate for the Rule of Law as a means to achieve sustainable development and peace.

questions.question: A 2 Ω resistance is connected to a 4 Ω resistance in series. Their equivalent resistance will be:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6 Ω**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• For resistors in series, **equivalent resistance adds directly**: **Rₑq = R₁ + R₂**.
 
• Substituting the values: **Rₑq = 2 Ω + 4 Ω =** **6 Ω**.
 
• In a series circuit, the **same current** flows through each resistor, so adding resistance increases total opposition to current.
 
• The result **6 Ω corresponds to Option 3**, which is larger than each individual resistance, as expected for series connections.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Resistance (R)**

 
 
• Measures how strongly a component opposes electric current.
 
• Unit is the **ohm** denoted by the Greek letter **Ω**.
 
• Depends on material resistivity, length, and cross-sectional area of the conductor.
 
• Measured using an ohmmeter or via V and I using Ohm’s law.
 
 
 
• **Series Connection**
 
 
• Components are connected end to end, forming a single path for current.
 
• **Current is the same** through all elements; voltages divide across them.
 
• Total or equivalent resistance is the **sum** of individual resistances.
 
• Characteristic check: Rₑq is always **greater than** any individual series resistor.
 
 
 
• **Equivalent Resistance**
 
 
• A single resistance that can replace a combination with the same V–I behavior at its terminals.
 
• For series: **Rₑq = R₁ + R₂ + R₃ + …**
 
• Contrast with parallel: **1/Rₑq = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ + …**, where Rₑq is less than the smallest branch.
 
• Useful for simplifying networks before applying circuit laws.
 
 
 
• **Ohm’s Law and Voltage Drops**
 
 
• Ohm’s law: **V = I R**, relates voltage, current, and resistance.
 
• In series, with current I, each drop is **Vₖ = I Rₖ**; the source voltage equals the sum of drops.
 
• Example check: if a 12 V source drives 2 Ω and 4 Ω in series, Rₑq = 6 Ω, so I = 12/6 = 2 A; drops are 4 V and 8 V.
 
• This verifies both the arithmetic and the distribution of voltages in series circuits.
 
 
 
• **Power Considerations**
 
 
• Power dissipated: **P = I²R = V²/R = V I**.
 
• In series, the higher resistance **dissipates more power** for the same current.
 
• For the example above at 2 A: P₂Ω = 8 W, P₄Ω = 16 W, total 24 W equals source power.
 
• Ensures component ratings are not exceeded during operation.

questions.question: The phenomenon due to which the relative motion between a conductor and a magnet produces a potential difference across the conductor is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**electromagnetic induction**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Electromagnetic induction** is the phenomenon due to which the relative motion between a conductor and a magnet produces a potential difference across the conductor.
 
• This principle was discovered by **Michael Faraday** in 1831.
 
• It forms the working basis of many electrical devices such as transformers, electric generators, and inductors.
 
• The induced potential difference or voltage is generated due to the changing magnetic field around the conductor.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Michael Faraday's** experiments showed that a change in the magnetic field within a closed loop of wire induces an electric current in the wire.
 
• The direction of the induced current is given by **Lenz's Law**, which states that the induced current will flow in such a direction that it will oppose the change in magnetic flux that produced it.
 
• The magnitude of the induced electromotive force (EMF) is given by **Faraday's Law of Induction**, which states that the EMF induced is proportional to the rate of change of magnetic flux.
 
• Applications of electromagnetic induction include electric power generation, induction cooking, wireless power transfer, and electromagnetic braking.

• They also introduced **Schedules XI and XII**, which enumerate the powers, authority, and responsibilities of Panchayats and Municipalities.
 
• The objective was to create a more inclusive and participatory form of governance by involving local communities in decision-making processes.
 
• These amendments have been instrumental in promoting **decentralization**, **accountability**, and **transparency** in local governance.
